item.title: WH adviser Hassett urges ‘discipline’ for Fed economists over tariff study
item.description: President Donald Trump’s top economist on Wednesday urged that Federal Reserve economists be punished for research last week that showed American companies and consumers paying for nearly all the new tariffs imposed by the White House last year. item.title: FDA will drop two-study requirement for new drug approvals, aiming to speed access
item.description: The Food and Drug Administration plans to drop its longtime standard of requiring two rigorous studies for new drug approvals. The change announced Wednesday is the latest move by Trump administration officials vowing to speed up the availability of medical products. Since the 1960s, the FDA has generally required that new drugs be shown safe and effective in two trials. item.title: DoorDash sees strong quarterly growth in sales and orders but warns of big costs
item.description: DoorDash's revenue rose 38% in the fourth quarter as it gained new U.S. customers and added new services like restaurant reservations. Total orders also rose 32% to 903 million, beating analysts’ forecasts. Investors cheered that growth, sending DoorDash’s stock up more than 13% in after-hours trading. item.title: Mamdani reboots homeless encampment sweeps in New York City
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has resumed the practice of clearing out homeless encampments, saying he has retooled the process. The Democratic mayor on Wednesday said the city’s homeless services department would lead the effort rather than having police handle the removal of encampments. The decision came as at least 19 people have died outside over several days of brutal cold in the city. The mayor's office says there's no evidence anyone who died had been living in encampments.
